A2 Key Paper 2 Listening Part 1 – Teacher’s Notes

 Description

In this lesson students do a lead-in activity in which they listen to a description of a person and identify
who it is. They answer some questions to familiarise themselves with A2 Key Paper 2 Listening Part 1
and underline the main words in Part 1 questions. Finally, they complete a Part 1 Listening task.

Time required:  20–30 minutes

Materials        Cut-up pictures from Part 1
required:        Handout 1 (2 pages)
                 Recording of A2 Key Listening sample paper Part 1
                 Follow-up activities - transcript Part 1 and answer sheet (optional)

Aims:            to familiarise students with the content and format of A2 Key Paper 2
                     Listening Part 1

                 to practise Part 1

Procedure

    1. Explain to your students that they will be doing Part 1 of the A2 Key Listening exam. As a lead-
         in explain that you are going to ask three students to stand up and that you are going to
         describe one of them. Your description could be something like this: ‘X has long dark curly hair.
         She doesn’t wear glasses. She’s very tall.’ Ask the class which students you have described.
         You could follow this with descriptions of three different bags, three different books etc. In
         groups of three or four ask students to take their mobile phones, pencil cases and bags out.
         Each student takes turns to describe one of them, the others compete to guess correctly. The
         idea here is to provide an activity which is similar to A2 Key Listening Part 1.

    2. Give out a copy of Handout 1 to each student. Ask students to look at the Part 1 task and elicit
         what candidates have to do in Part 1 by asking these questions:

         How many conversations will you hear? (5)
         How many questions are there for each conversation? (One)
         How do you choose the answer? (Choose A, B or C for the correct picture on the question

             paper, while you listen. When you listen for the second time, check your answer.)
         When do you write your answers on the answer sheet? (At the end of the test)

    3. Photocopy question 1 of the sample task and enlarge it to A3 size (if possible), put the pictures

on the board and ask students in pairs to decide where the places are.
 A – museum (art exhibition)
 B – hairdresser
 C – café

4. Write on the board ‘Where will Claire meet Alex?’ Ask your students to work in pairs and decide

what the important words are in the sentence.

Answer: Where Claire  meet                     Alex

5. Tell students you are now going to play the recording and they must decide what the answer is.
    Allow them to check in pairs before open class feedback (see Answer key).

6. Before you play the recording for questions 2–5, ask students to read the questions and
    underline the key vocabulary so they know what they are listening for. This emphasises the
    importance of reading the questions carefully.

7. Allow them to check in pairs before open class feedback. Check which words students have
    underlined (see Answer key).

8. Divide the class into two teams, and then put the three pictures for question 2 on the board.
    Explain that you are going to play the recording for question 2 twice and then one representative
    from each team goes and stands next to and points to the correct picture. Each team
    representative will get one point for the correct answer (see Answer key).

9. Tell your learners they are now going to do questions 3–5. Elicit from them what they need to do
     in each pause between the conversations in the real exam (underline key vocabulary). Play the
     recording without stopping. Allow your students to check their answers with their partner before
     open class feedback. As you monitor you can hear if they had any problems with the vocabulary
     and address when going through the answers (see Answer key).

10. As a round-up, ask students what type of information they listened for in each question.
     Answers
     1. a place
     2. a time
     3. a date
     4. the weather
     5. a price

Point out that these are typical of the things that are tested in Part 1. Elicit what other typical
things might be described for Part 1 tasks.
Suggested answers: people, animals, objects, activities, countries, months, etc.

Suggested follow-up activities
           1. Photocopy the transcript for Part 1. Students could work in pairs and read out the dialogues.
                   They could then highlight the part of the dialogue where they can find the answers to the
                   questions.
           2. If you want the students to practise using the answer sheet, photocopy it and ask the
                   students to fill in the lozenges in pencil for their answers to Part 1.
